title: spora: A Unified Multimodal Dataset for Spatial Proteomics
claim: A unified dataset, its access library, and a benchmark suite fit together as one resource for training and evaluating foundation models.
layout: 3 panels: dataset stats top-left, pipeline top-right, benchmark row bottom; icons
description: A three-part composite figure. Panel a (top left, 'spora [data]') opens with a row of icon-plus-number headline statistics: 13,546 images, 5,477 patients, 35 cohorts, 14 tissue origins and 5 technologies. Below are a horizontal bar chart of tiles per tissue origin on a log scale, and two stacked bars for technology share and H&E pairing. A row of file icons lists the per-sample files: images, masks, cell types and metadata. Panel b (top right, 'spora [io]') is a vertical flow of four steps joined by arrows: dataset browser, tiling and sampling, multimodal lazy loading, and standardization. Each step has a small thumbnail and a short description. Panel c (bottom, 'spora [bench]') has four columns of benchmark tasks. Each column shows a mini model schematic, a list of models and a list of cohorts. Blue shades mark foundation models versus task-specific models. The eye goes first to the large numbers at top left.
caption: Overview of \spora. a. Unified dataset composition and per-sample file structure of \sporadata. b. Library pipeline of \sporaio from dataset browsing and tiling to standardized model input. c. \sporabench benchmark tasks for foundation model evaluation.
abstract: Spatial proteomics (SP) captures the molecular composition and spatial organization of tissues at single-cell resolution, opening a direct view of the cellular ecosystems that drive disease. Protein panels, acquisition platforms, and tissue contexts differ from one cohort to the next, and a coherent picture of tissue biology can only emerge from models trained to bridge this heterogeneity. Foundation models offer the natural path forward, but their training depends on large, harmonized corpora that span platforms, panels, and cohorts. No public resource currently approaches that scale; available data sit in small, narrowly scoped releases with incompatible formats and conventions. We present spora, a large-scale multimodal SP dataset of 13,546 standardized multiplex images from 5,477 patients across 35 cohorts and five major SP technologies. Curated with biomedical experts, spora provides model-training-ready formats together with cell and tissue segmentations, structured clinical metadata, and, where available, paired H&E enabling the training of virtual staining models. It is complemented by spora [io], a unified interface for tiling, sampling, and standardization across all cohorts and modalities, and spora [bench], a benchmark suite spanning cell phenotyping, diagnostic and therapeutic prediction as well as virtual staining tasks across twelve cohorts that places current SP foundation models on common ground against task-specific baselines.
